steps: Derive a UTF-8 validation predicate from RFC3629 and explain why successful construction proves byte encoding only while the backing bytes remain live and unchanged.

State storage lifetime and mutation restrictions explicitly, including a safe constructed example where another alias changes a previously validated buffer.

Record that Python decoding is an independent implementation, not a proof of normalization or all higher-level text properties.

units.title: Construct: Branded pool handles with checked generations
steps: Separate nominal handle category, pool identity, slot generation and ownership; demonstrate why a C wrapper cannot create a compile-time fresh brand per runtime pool or enforce linear use.

Derive FREE/LIVE/RETIRED transitions and count available slots. Explain why copying a handle is permitted by C yet does not duplicate ownership. Pool objects must remain live at fixed addresses and cannot be reinitialized or reused while handles survive: pointer identity does not prevent ABA across object lifetimes. Compare PhantomData nominal/lifetime roles without claiming equivalent static checks.
checks: A handle frompoolA is rejected bypoolB; release/reacquire invalidates the old generation; release atUINT_MAX retires its slot and reduces usable capacity to3.

Run adt.brands and enumerate short acquire/release/get traces against an independent occupancy/generation model. Kill owner-check omission and generation-check omission independently. Compile a wrong-category handle probe; show that copying or explicitly constructing a valid public representation bypasses any unforgeability claim.
